title: North Pacific oxygen loss on sigma0 26.0-26.7 (2009-2025 vs 1984-1996) equals a 0.06-0.11 kg/m3 lighter AOU-profile shift, 40-70% of winter surface lightening; CalCOFI nitrate drifted vs GLODAP
abstract: Question: is the winter surface lightening at the North Pacific outcrop large enough to explain the oxygen (O2) loss on sigma0 26.0-26.7 along the North Pacific Current and off California? Approach: if surface water becomes lighter by delta and pathways do not change, water now on sigma was ventilated where sigma + delta outcropped, so pathway tracers obey P_late(sigma) = P_ref(sigma + delta). We fitted this equivalent density shift to cell-matched AOU, nitrate and phosphate changes (2009-2025 minus 1984-1996) in World Ocean Database ship data, GLODAPv2.2023 and the CalCOFI bottle database, with cruise bootstraps, and compared it with the measured winter surface lightening of 0.148 kg/m3 (30-50 N, 140 E-150 W; sci:84f111c0). Results: O2 at sigma0 26.5 fell by 10-24 umol/kg, with O2 solubility changes below 2 umol/kg. Along 28-42 N from 180 to California the AOU change equals a shift of 0.06-0.105 kg/m3 (WOD; CalCOFI 0.100, 0.090-0.105), 41-71% of the surface lightening; a full shift would give 7-27 umol/kg more AOU than observed. Off 130-180 W the 26.5 water became cooler and fresher, the signature of surface warming. The CalCOFI shift rose from 0.01 in 1995-1999 to 0.10 after 2010 and was also positive in 1950-1969; its lag behind the surface index (3-13 yr, r 0.63-0.70) is not significant against surrogates (p = 0.13). Shift and AOU-proportional shapes both fit the fit range; on held-out denser levels the shift is better in 21 of 21 cases, on lighter levels in 7 of 22. An apparent CalCOFI nitrate deficit (nitrate/AOU kappa 0.44) is not in GLODAP (0.88) and agrees with a -0.92 umol/kg change of the CalCOFI-minus-GLODAP nitrate crossover offset between 1985-1994 and 2011-2016. Interpretation: surface lightening is sufficient in size; models need an outcrop of these classes and about 0.15 kg/m3 lightening. Limitations: one surface box, pathways assumed fixed, slowdown not excluded, few GLODAP cruises, no model O2 used.

display.caption: AOU change (2009-2025 minus 1984-1996) against sigma0 in four regions, with 95% cruise-bootstrap bands, the fitted density shift (dashed), the shift equal to the surface lightening of 0.148 kg/m3 (dotted) and a change proportional to AOU (yellow). Grey band: fit range 26.0-26.7.

Equivalent density shift of AOU (top) and nitrate (bottom) by region and data set, with 95% intervals, against the winter surface lightening 0.148 (0.131-0.171) kg/m3. CalCOFI and WOD bottle nitrate near California include the CalCOFI nitrate offset.

Left: equivalent AOU shift in 5-yr windows (and single CalCOFI years) against 1984-1996, with the winter surface lightening of the ship index (5-yr means). Right: cell-matched AOU change at sigma0 26.5. Grey: reference period.

citations.reason: We use its public winter surface density index as the independent lightening and test whether the outcrop change it found is large enough to give the oxygen loss.
We adapt its WOD extraction code and use the same longitude bands; our 1997-2008 shifts were larger in the east than near 180, which a simple eastward advection does not explain.
Its within-water-type loss off California is equal to a partial density shift of the ventilated AOU structure in our analysis.
Model O2 changes off California quoted in the consistency argument.
Float evidence of continued offshore loss with nitrate gain; our nutrient ratio test agrees offshore within wide intervals.
Float evidence that the transition-zone loss persisted after 2006.
CMIP6 models change oxygen less than observed; our transfer fraction gives a quantity models must reproduce.
CalCOFI sigma0 26.5 oxygen low; our CalCOFI equivalent shift series describes the same low.
Earlier sigma 26.5 study in the same campaign thread.
Tracer-age attribution was unreliable, so we use a tracer-free density-shift test.
